clue.text: Noisy medley for four voices

indicators.note: a medley is a jumbled mixture, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A loud piece of music arranged for a vocal quartet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' looks like a musical term for the quartet's piece, but it signals that FOURVOICES is rearranged; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vociferous shouts loudly and insistently, so the word means clamorous or noisy.

clue.text: Wide boy backed by these bigshots

indicators.note: backed tells you the word for the wide boy is written backwards

parts.note: a spiv is a flashy petty crook, British slang 'wide boy'

explanation.surface: A flashy small-time crook is supported by important people.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv or wide boy is British slang for a flashy petty dealer; 'backed' reverses SPIV. 'by these' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: VIPs, very important persons, are notables or celebrities.

clue.text: So costly a victory makes an outsider poor

parts.note: a cad, in old slang, was an outsider, an ill-bred man
mean can mean poor or shabby

explanation.surface: A win that costs so much reduces a stranger to poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cadmean victory, like a Pyrrhic one, ruins the victor; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cadmean victory is one won at ruinous cost to the winner, after the story of Cadmus.

clue.text: Patient diggers might regard him as heaven-sent

definitions.text: Patient diggers might regard him as heaven-sent

parts.words: Patient diggers might regard him as heaven-sent
parts.note: diggers are Australian miners or Australians, here sick ones in the outback for whom help arrives from the sky

explanation.surface: Miners waiting patiently would think a certain man a godsend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diggers' is slang for Australians; 'Patient' is a noun-adjective meaning sick people; the medic arrives by plane from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's outback medical service sends physicians by aircraft to remote patients.

clue.text: The bigger of two bottle kings

definitions.text: The bigger of two bottle kings

parts.words: The bigger of two bottle kings
parts.note: two kings of Israel lent their names to large wine bottles; the larger one holds six standard bottles

explanation.surface: Asks which of two kings of the bottle is the larger.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeroboam and his successor both name champagne bottles; Jeroboam holds four bottles, the one wanted six.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a wine bottle holding six standard bottles, named after a king of Judah.

clue.text: Mischievous sea-creature

definitions.meaning: a mischievous child or scamp; the word is a noun used for such a youngster
the spiny sea creature, short for its full name

explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a mischievous child, and the spiny echinoderm is a sea urchin.

clue.text: Recognized something fresh-sounding

indicators.note: the clue says the letters are the sound of the preceding words, not their spelling

parts.note: something fresh is new

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a thing that had a novel ring to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' tells you to say NEW aloud and spell it as the past tense of 'know'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recognized a person is to have known them on sight; past tense of 'know'.

clue.text: Having reached match-point?

parts.note: a match here is a marriage, so the point reached is the wedding

explanation.surface: A tennis player is one point from winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match-point' suggests tennis, but the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding, the moment a marriage match is made.

clue.text: A tornado at sea, a gargoyle on land

definitions.meaning: a whirling column of water drawn up from the sea
a spout carrying rainwater from a roof, as a gargoyle does

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a marine whirlwind lifting a water column and a pipe discharging rain from a roof.

clue.text: With which playful slap an old man made the infants sing

definitions.text: With which playful slap an old man made the infants sing

parts.words: With which playful slap an old man made the infants sing
parts.note: points to the nursery song 'This Old Man', whose chorus runs 'knick-knack, ... give a dog a bone', a word that is also a playful smack

explanation.surface: A grandfather's light-hearted smack sets the children singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The children's counting song 'This Old Man' has the refrain 'knick-knack paddywhack', and a paddywhack is also a mild slap.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddywhack is a smack or spanking, and the word is famous from a children's song refrain.

clue.text: Spinners return to the locality

indicators.note: return asks for the word for spinners to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: spinning tops are toys that spin

explanation.surface: Bowlers who turn the ball come back to their home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinners' suggests cricket bowlers, but here they are toy tops; 'return' reverses TOPS. 'to the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular place or neighbourhood, the same as a locality.

clue.text: Car workers who excel at Radio/Tv parlour games ?

definitions.meaning: people who hammer out dents in car bodywork

definitions.text: who excel at Radio/Tv parlour games ?
definitions.meaning: people who defeat the panel on a quiz show

explanation.definitionFit: These mechanics repair vehicle bodywork; read literally they defeat panels, the teams on broadcast quiz shows.

clue.text: Show boat man when King Edward joined the Navy ?

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
ER, Edward Rex, is the royal cipher of King Edward
N is a standard abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A question about a sailor on a show boat in the days when a King Edward signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome Kern wrote the music for the musical 'Show Boat', so the 'man' is its composer, not a crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was the American composer of the musical Show Boat.

clue.text: One tribe captured in the bush by this officer

indicators.note: the first pieces are held prisoner inside the word for the bush

parts.note: a brier is a thorny bush
the Roman numeral for one is I
Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: An army officer has taken a member of a tribe prisoner in the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured in' puts I and GAD inside BRIER, after its first two letters; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is an army officer ranking above a colonel, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: He's much as Cora made out -a bragging poltroon

indicators.note: made out means construed or reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man is just as Cora described him: a boastful coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' rearranges MUCHASCORA. Scaramouch is the stock boastful coward of Italian comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaramouch is the cowardly braggart of the commedia dell'arte.

clue.text: Diana can change nationality

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters in the two names before it

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A woman called Diana is able to take a new citizenship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like part of the story about switching citizenship but rearranges DIANACAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Canadian is the nationality of a citizen of Canada.

clue.text: Early morning drink? Depends on the throat

parts.note: dew forms in the early morning
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A dawn drink, and then an odd remark that it relies on one's throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends' is used in its old sense of 'hangs down', so the definition describes a fold of skin hanging from the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewlap is the loose fold of skin that hangs beneath the throat of cattle or some birds.

clue.text: Herrick liked it in dressing

parts.note: the poet Robert Herrick wrote 'Delight in' a sweet untidiness of dress

explanation.surface: A poet's preference in clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Herrick's poem 'Delight in Disorder' opens 'A sweet disorder in the dress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidiness or lack of order; Herrick praised it in clothes.

clue.text: Florid style of gold returned by two companies

indicators.note: returned asks for the heraldic word for gold to be read backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: two asks for the abbreviation that follows to be written twice

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An ornate golden style is sent back by a pair of firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns OR into RO; 'two' doubles CO. 'of' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo was an ornate eighteenth-century decorative fashion full of curves and scrollwork.

clue.text: Guardian dog upset the duty list

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the word for the duty list upside down

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A guard dog has knocked over the work schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses ROTA to ATOR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper who looks after a museum's collection.

clue.text: Faraway place to send the boy, but U.K. unsettling

parts.note: Tim is a typical boy's name

indicators.note: unsettling means the letters of the next two words are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written as its two letters

explanation.surface: Banishing a lad to a remote spot is upsetting for the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' rearranges BUTUK to give BUKTU. 'to send' is a link; Timbuktu is the proverbial distant place.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbuktu, in Mali, is used proverbially for the most remote place imaginable.

clue.text: One of those things one has at one's fingers' ends

definitions.text: One of those things one has at one's fingers' ends

parts.words: One of those things one has at one's fingers' ends
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'at one's fingertips', but means literally the joints of the fingers

explanation.surface: Something one knows thoroughly, at one's fingertips.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests expert knowledge; literally the joints of the fingers are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle is a finger joint, found toward the ends of the fingers.

clue.text: Doctor Lake meets the Fire God

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A doctor at a lakeside encounters a deity of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Moloch was a Canaanite deity to whom children were sacrificed by fire.

clue.text: Traveller returned to study under pressure-no horseplay!

indicators.note: returned asks for the word for intense studying to be read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to study hard under pressure of an exam
O is nought, nothing
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A traveller comes back to revise urgently, with a ban on rough fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns CRAM into MARC; 'horseplay' is not rowdiness but a game played on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian explorer who journeyed to China in the thirteenth century.

clue.text: Lean against a water-container, say

indicators.note: say tells you the letters are spelt as the preceding words are pronounced

parts.note: a butt is a large barrel for collecting rainwater

explanation.surface: Someone props themselves on a rain barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A water butt is a barrel catching rain from a gutter; said aloud, 'a butt' gives the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or rest against something, as one building leans on another.

clue.text: First subject of Virgil's song and Shaw's play

definitions.text: First subject of Virgil's song and Shaw's play

parts.words: First subject of Virgil's song and Shaw's play
parts.note: the Aeneid opens 'Arma virumque cano', and Shaw borrowed that for a play title about war and the man

explanation.surface: A literary question about where Virgil and Shaw begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aeneid begins 'Of arms and the man I sing', and Shaw's comedy is 'Arms and the Man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons are the first thing Virgil's epic sings of, echoed in Shaw's title.

clue.text: As far as this, this ward is unlucky

indicators.note: this points to the word 'ward', saying the word for unlucky is read only as far as that point

parts.note: untoward means unfortunate or unlucky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that this hospital ward has bad luck, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: UNTOWARD (unlucky) taken only as far as 'this ward', that is with WARD cut off, leaves the old word for 'up to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an archaic preposition meaning to or until, up to a limit.

clue.text: One that goes barking up trees for its grub ?

definitions.text: One that goes barking up trees for its grub ?

parts.words: One that goes barking up trees for its grub ?
parts.note: barking means stripping at bark, not yelping like a dog, so the creature drills tree bark for insect larvae

explanation.surface: A dog barking up the wrong tree in search of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking up trees' suggests a dog, but the bird pecks at bark; its grub is a beetle larva as well as food.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird hammers into tree bark with its beak to find insect larvae.

clue.text: Running companion for devious hunters

parts.note: points to the paper-chase game in which hounds follow a twisting trail laid by one runner

explanation.surface: A jogging partner for crafty huntsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game hare and hounds, one runner lays a winding trail and the pack chases them; the hare is also the animal hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the cross-country game of hare and hounds, the runner laying the trail is so called.

clue.text: Installed singers

parts.note: read 'installed' as 'in stalled', singers who sit in the choir stalls of a church

explanation.surface: Vocalists who have been put into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Installed' is split as in-stalled: church singers sit in the choir stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a church choir sit in the choir stalls of the chancel.
